title: Homogeneous bases for Frobenius modules with lattice weights
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] of prime characteristic $p>0$, and define $A=k_\sigma[F]$ to consist of finite sums $\sum_{r\geq0}a_rF^r$, with coefficientwise addition and multiplication $(aF^r)(bF^t)=ab^{p^r}F^{r+t}$. Let $d,s\geq0$. Let $M$ be a left $A$-module admitting a basis with $d$ elements, meaning that it is isomorphic to $A^d$ with coordinatewise left multiplication. Restriction of scalars along the constant polynomials makes $M$ a $k$-vector space. Suppose there are $k$-linear subspaces $M_
u$ for $
u\in\mathbf Z^s$ such that $M= igoplus_{
u\in\mathbf Z^s}M_
u$ as a $k$-vector space (every element has a unique finite decomposition) and $F(M_
u)\subseteq M_{p
u}$ for every $
u$. Then there are elements $f_1,\ldots,f_d$ forming a left $A$-basis of $M$, and weights $
u_1,\ldots,
u_d\in\mathbf Z^s$, with $f_j\in M_{
u_j}$ for every $j$. No perfectness assumption is imposed on $k$. The cases $d=0$ and $s=0$, and weight zero, are included.

proof.text:
Put $N= igoplus_{
u
e0}M_
u$. Since $p
u=0$ if and only if $
u=0$, both $M_0$ and $N$ are left $A$-submodules and $M=M_0\oplus N$ as left modules. The two coordinate projections commute with $k$ and $F$, hence with $A$. Project the given $d$ generators: each summand is finitely generated. Via the supplied isomorphism $M\simeq A^d$, each summand is a finitely generated left submodule of a free module. Apply [lem-sfb-frobenius-skew-free-submodules] to obtain finite $A$-bases $(a_1,\ldots,a_t)$ of $M_0$ and $(e_1,\ldots,e_r)$ of $N$. Every $a_i$ is homogeneous of weight zero. The hypotheses permit the same imperfect field $k$; no division by Frobenius on $k$ is involved.

This refinement is not stated in Milne; its independent argument is recorded in the delivery report. No Stacks tag is asserted. Separate weight zero and use the ungraded freeness input.

proof.text:
Write $J=\operatorname{span}_k F(N)$. In the $k$-basis $(F^q e_i)_{q\geq0,1\leq i\leq r}$ of $N$, one has $F(\sum c_{iq}F^qe_i)=\sum c_{iq}^pF^{q+1}e_i$. Thus $J$ is exactly the span of the terms with $q\geq1$, and $N/J$ has dimension $r$. In particular it is the span of $F(N)$, not necessarily the set $F(N)$. Decomposing each input into its homogeneous parts shows $J$ is the sum of its homogeneous components: the weight-$
u$ part is the span of $F(N_{
u/p})$ if $
u\in p\mathbf Z^s$, and is zero otherwise. Hence $N/J$ is internally graded. Choose a basis in each of its nonzero weight components and lift it homogeneously; their union is a basis $( ar b_1,\ldots, ar b_r)$, since the quotient is finite-dimensional. To see this choice is finite, decompose a finite spanning set into homogeneous parts, select bases from those finite spanning parts in each weight, and use directness. Denote the lifts by $b_j$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dilating-weight-nakayama] with $V=N$, $T(v)=Fv$, and $\sigma(c)=c^p$. Additivity and $T(cv)=c^pT(v)$ are the module law for $Fc=c^pF$. The grading of $N$ has zero component zero, and $T(N_\nu)\subseteq N_{p\nu}$ is the given hypothesis. The $b_j$ are homogeneous and their cosets span $N/J$ by step 2. The cited conclusion says $N$ is spanned over $k$ by all $F^q b_j$. Expanding a coefficient of $A$ as a finite sum $\sum_q c_qF^q$ now says exactly that $(b_j)$ generates $N$ as a left $A$-module.

proof.text: In the given free-module coordinates $M\simeq A^d$, use the $k$-coordinates indexed by $(i,q)$, $1\leq i\leq d$, $q\geq0$. The operator $F$ raises each coefficient to its $p$-th power and moves coordinate $(i,q)$ to $(i,q+1)$. Frobenius on a field is an injective ring homomorphism: $a^p=b^p$ implies $(a-b)^p=0$ and hence $a=b$. Therefore [lem-sfb-coefficient-endomorphism-preserves-independence] shows that applying $F$ to any finite $k$-independent family in $M$ leaves it independent; shifting all coordinates by one preserves independence because a relation can be read back in the old coordinates. This applies in particular to families in $N$.

source.place: Agent algebraic refinement supporting Proposition 14.50, printed p.296, and the homogeneous Frobenius-module prerequisite in the vector-group argument. This refinement is not stated in Milne; its independent argument is recorded in the delivery report. No Stacks tag is asserted. Coefficient-semilinear independence; never assume Frobenius is onto.

proof.text: Induct on $R\geq0$ to show $(F^q b_j)_{0\leq q\leq R,1\leq j\leq r}$ is $k$-independent. At $R=0$, reduce a relation modulo $J$ and use that the $\bar b_j$ form a basis. For the inductive step reduce a relation modulo $J$ again: its $q=0$ coefficients vanish. The remaining vectors are the $F$-images of the independent family for $R-1$, so step 4 kills every remaining coefficient. Every finite left $A$-relation among the $b_j$ expands to one of these finite $k$-relations; thus $(b_j)$ is an $A$-basis by step 3. Concatenating it with $(a_i)$ gives a homogeneous $A$-basis of $M$. For any finite $A$-basis $(u_i)$, the quotient $M/\operatorname{span}_kF(M)$ has as $k$-basis the cosets of $u_i$, by the same coefficient computation as step 2. The given basis shows its dimension is $d$, so $t+r=d$. Relabel the concatenated basis as $f_1,\ldots,f_d$ and retain its weights. Empty bases and $s=0$ are covered: then $N=0$.
